source: Fleming (2001) Recombinant uncertainty in technological search (AcaWiki summary page only)
finding: Baseline for the machine studies. Patent data; usefulness is incoming citations; components are patent subclasses. Familiar components raise usefulness. Refining a familiar combination raises usefulness and cuts uncertainty. Cumulative reuse of a combination lowers usefulness. New combinations have lower mean and higher variance.
numbers: Summary hypothesis results: familiar components raise usefulness (supported); familiar components lower uncertainty (not supported); refining familiar combos raises usefulness and lowers uncertainty (supported); cumulative use lowers usefulness (supported). Page says cited 340+ times. No coefficients or N on the page.
limits: Only a wiki summary was opened, no coefficients or sample size. The machine studies below mostly do not test the reuse penalty or the familiar-component effect directly.
agent_relevance: Gives the target pattern to look for in LLM work: mean falls and spread grows with distance, and reuse of one combination decays.

source: Liu, Dubova, Conklin, Harada, Griffiths (2026) Assessing the Effect of Cross-Domain Mapping on Creativity in Humans and LLMs
finding: Closest direct LLM test of the distance and usefulness pattern. Humans and 7 LLMs designed products from a random source domain (cross-domain mapping) or from an unmet user need. LLMs were more original than humans in both conditions. Mapping helped humans but gave no average gain to LLMs.
numbers: Humans N=140 writers, 1002 raters. LLMs: o3, Claude-Sonnet-4, gpt-4o, gemini-2.5-pro, deepseek-v3, Llama-3.3-70b, Qwen2.5-72B. Human originality 2.93 (mapping) vs 2.57 (user need). o3 3.83 and Claude-Sonnet-4 3.76 in mapping. Mapping effect overall beta=0.36 (p<.001); condition x source interaction beta=0.48 (p<.001).
limits: Product design only; human ratings on 1-5 scales; semantic distance computed from Wikipedia text.
agent_relevance: Supplying a random far source does not help a strong LLM on average. O7 should not use random analogues on routine problems.

source: Liu, Dubova, Conklin, Harada, Griffiths (2026) Assessing the Effect of Cross-Domain Mapping on Creativity in Humans and LLMs
finding: Distance moderates the benefit. Originality rose with source-target semantic distance for both humans and LLMs. Pooled LLMs lost to the user-need baseline at first and only matched it once the closest 20% of pairs were cut. The two best LLMs gained only from the far half.
numbers: Distance-originality slope: humans b=.1 (p<.01), LLMs b=.18 (p<.001). o3 + Claude-Sonnet-4 mapping effect: all pairs b=0.02 (p=.64); top 50% most distant b=0.12 (p=.029); top 10% b=0.24 (p=.024).
limits: Post-hoc exclusion of near pairs; effect sizes in rating units; only the top two models show a gain.
agent_relevance: Supports far analogues only at impasses or in open mode, and only for strong models. Distance can be computed in code with embeddings.

source: Liu, Dubova, Conklin, Harada, Griffiths (2026) Assessing the Effect of Cross-Domain Mapping on Creativity in Humans and LLMs
finding: Variance and cost side of Fleming holds for humans, much less for LLMs. The top 10% most original human ideas under mapping were less useful and less feasible. Equally original LLM ideas did not pay that cost.
numbers: Top-10% human vs LLM ideas under mapping: originality equal (b=0.02, p=.63); feasibility lower for humans (b=0.26, p=.045); investment-worthiness lower (0.60, p<.001); utility lower (0.81, p<.001). Example: pickle desk, originality 4.78/5, utility 1.22/5.
limits: Selected on the tail, so part of the effect is selection. LLM output may be less extreme because it is trained to be sensible.
agent_relevance: Low mean, high spread appears in humans; LLMs seem to get originality with less usefulness loss. A usefulness filter is still needed after far mapping.

source: Liu, Dubova, Conklin, Harada, Griffiths (2026) Assessing the Effect of Cross-Domain Mapping on Creativity in Humans and LLMs
finding: Humans and LLMs transfer different things from a source. Humans carry over surface features; LLMs carry over structure and function. Asking an LLM to act as a lazy human did not change this; asking it to act as an artist attentive to perception moved it toward surface mapping.
numbers: Qualitative coding plus a preliminary prompt probe; no counts in the text read.
limits: Preliminary prompt probe, small. Example: pickle car, humans propose green paint.
agent_relevance: Which features to attend to matters more than effort. O7 should name the mapping type (structural or functional) in the prompt.

source: Shen, Druckmann, Zou (2026) Unlocking LLM Creativity in Science through Analogical Reasoning
finding: LLMs collapse to few approaches on open-ended research problems. Asking for cross-domain solutions barely helps. Analogical reasoning (AR: build an analogy from shared relational structure, then search for a solution in the analogue) gives far more diverse and novel solutions.
numbers: Solution Vendi score up 90-173% and domain Vendi up 100-115% over baselines; 3.5x more unique domains, 1.3x more unique solutions than next best. 50 research problems, 5 solutions each, 3 LLMs. Binary novelty (no-domain / cross-domain / AR): Claude 1.6/21.6/50.4%; GPT 8.8/27.2/58.8%; Gemini 8.6/37.9/68.8%.
limits: Novelty is LLM-judged against retrieved papers (Claude Sonnet 4.5 judge); human validation is moderate.
agent_relevance: A typed analogy step (O7) beats just saying go to another domain. Cross-domain recall alone collapses.

source: Shen, Druckmann, Zou (2026) Unlocking LLM Creativity in Science through Analogical Reasoning
finding: Analogue distance rises under AR and analogy novelty is highest there, while structural depth stays similar across settings.
numbers: Domain distance for AR 6.99 / 6.83 / 7.53 (Claude, GPT, Gemini) vs no-domain 2.29 / 3.08 / 3.37, over 3x. Structural depth 7.06 to 8.60 in all settings. AR analogy novelty 4.82 / 5.27 / 5.58, above even the ground-truth analogy. Human-LLM agreement 88.6% (distance), 75.7% (novelty).
limits: LLM-judged scores; agreement figures are for the judge, not for solution quality.
agent_relevance: Analogue distance can be measured by a judge or embeddings, and depth must be checked so that far matches are not shallow.

source: Shen, Druckmann, Zou (2026) Unlocking LLM Creativity in Science through Analogical Reasoning
finding: Usefulness check: AR solutions were implemented on four biomedical tasks with gains. A human pairwise study found AR solutions more novel and mostly reasonable.
numbers: Humans judged the AR solution more novel than the cross-domain solution 78% of the time (kappa=0.445); reasonable 67% of the time. Perturbation effect prediction MMD PCA 1.65 to 0.13 (about 13x) via an economics finite-mixture analogy; brain-region interaction Spearman 0.729 to published methods.
limits: Four chosen case studies, no failure rate; 67% reasonable means a third were not.
agent_relevance: A far analogue produced a real working method, but a third of ideas were judged unreasonable, so a code check of the mapping is still required.

source: Si, Yang, Hashimoto (2024) Can LLMs Generate Novel Research Ideas? A Large-Scale Human Study
finding: Blinded expert review: LLM ideas judged more novel than expert human ideas, with no significant loss in feasibility. But the LLM agent produced very few distinct ideas.
numbers: 49 idea writers, 79 reviewers, 298 reviews, 49 ideas per condition. Novelty 4.84 human, 5.64 AI (p<0.01), 5.81 AI + human rerank (p<0.001). Feasibility 6.61 / 6.34 / 6.44 (n.s.). Excitement 4.55 / 5.19 / 5.46. Of 4000 seed ideas per topic only about 200 (5%) were non-duplicates at cosine 0.8.
limits: 7 prompting-based NLP topics; reviewer agreement 56.1%; ideas not executed; best LLM judge 53.3% accuracy on this task.
agent_relevance: The 5% non-duplicate rate is the machine version of Fleming's reuse penalty: repeated sampling reuses the same combination. Dedupe by embedding before ranking.

source: Si, Hashimoto, Yang (2025) The Ideation-Execution Gap: Execution Outcomes of LLM-Generated versus Human Research Ideas
finding: Boundary condition on novelty gains. After 43 experts spent 100+ hours executing ideas, LLM ideas lost far more score than human ideas, erasing the novelty gap.
numbers: Score change after execution (1-10 scale): human novelty -0.010, excitement +0.078, effectiveness -0.052; AI ideas -1.049, -1.760, -1.879. Review-level N=181: humans higher on excitement, effectiveness, soundness, overall, not novelty. Idea-level N=43: no significant difference on any execution score.
limits: Low power at idea level; NLP prompting ideas only.
agent_relevance: Novel combinations look good on paper and fail on execution. The agent needs a code or test check before trusting a novel combination.

source: Mizrahi, Shani, Stanovsky, Jurafsky, Shahaf (2025) Cooking Up Creativity: Enhancing LLM Creativity through Structured Recombination
finding: Recombination scaffold: translate dishes to trees, recombine trees by cognitively inspired edits, filter by a value threshold, rank by novelty, translate back. Beat GPT-4o on novelty and diversity at a cost to value.
numbers: 48 human participants, 2 experiments. Novelty 3.53 vs GPT-4o 3.146 (p=0.0009) in Exp 1; 3.612 vs 3.141 (p=9.2e-8) in Exp 2. Rated valuable: 80% vs 82% (Exp 1), 85% vs 98% (Exp 2). Tree distance 132.14 vs 89.35 (p=3.6e-5) and 140.25 vs 129.55. Value threshold 0.3.
limits: One domain (recipes); value is a constraint and novelty the objective by design.
agent_relevance: Template for O7: value as constraint, novelty as objective, structured representation for the recombination step. Value dropped 13 points in Exp 2.

source: Mizrahi, Shani, Stanovsky, Jurafsky, Shahaf (2025) Cooking Up Creativity: Enhancing LLM Creativity through Structured Recombination
finding: GPT-4o fixates on the same parts and the same pattern when asked to fuse two items: it makes the first item with the second on the side. Structured recombination avoids it.
numbers: GPT-4o recipes: 56% used smoked paprika vs 0.375% in the repository; 47% mint; 41% maple syrup; 29% pomegranate molasses. Mean similarity to nearest corpus recipe 0.774 (Dish COVER) vs 0.851 (GPT-4o); 91% of Dish COVER under 0.85 vs 47% of GPT-4o; 38% under 0.75 vs 0%.
limits: Embedding similarity; recipe domain only.
agent_relevance: An LLM reuses the same few components and the same combination pattern, so reuse needs an explicit count and cap.

source: Hernandez, Brinkmann, Serna, Rahaman, Abu Alhaija, Yakura, Sola, Scholkopf, Rahwan (2024) Alien Recombination: Exploring Concept Blends Beyond Human Cognitive Availability in Visual Art
finding: Raising temperature easily makes new combinations, but not combinations no artist has used. Explicit ranking by cognitive unavailability (low probability under an artist-level model) does.
numbers: 50 input sequences, 150 outputs per temperature, temperatures 0.1 to 3.1. Above temperature 1, 85% of combinations had at least one new concept at artwork level; at temperature 3 more than half had zero cognitively unavailable concepts. Alien sampling (alpha=0.85) judged more novel by GPT-4 and by ResNet152 similarity.
limits: GPT-2-sized models; novelty judged by GPT-4 and embeddings, no human evaluation; DALL-E images stay in-distribution.
agent_relevance: Distance in concept space is computable in code with two cheap language models; random temperature is not a substitute for a distance-targeted search.

source: Cross-reading of Mizrahi et al. (2025) and Hernandez et al. (2024)
finding: Both papers treat recombination as an explicit ranked search over parts, with a familiarity or value score on each pair, instead of asking the model to be creative.
numbers: Alien: perplexity from two GPT-2 models ranks combinations. Dish COVER: surprise measure with value threshold 0.3.
limits: Interpretation across two sources, not a measured result.
agent_relevance: O7 recipe: enumerate pairs, score familiarity and value, then select the unfamiliar but valid ones.

source: Tang, Yang (2026) AI Research Agents Narrow Scientific Exploration
finding: Agent frameworks told to explore beyond seed papers still stay closer to them than later human work does. Local recombination dominates.
numbers: 219,655 ideas, 12 fields, 155 areas, 5 frameworks, 5 LLMs. Exploration distance 0.322 AI vs 0.410 human follow-on (all years 0.318 vs 0.399). Breadth 0.554 vs 0.599 (7.5% lower). Frontier alignment 0.045 lower pooled. Literature search reduced the gap.
limits: Embedding distances; human baseline is papers that cite the seeds; no execution test.
agent_relevance: Even with instructions to be bold, agents recombine near the start. Far distance must be forced by the procedure, not requested in words.

source: Tang, Yang (2026) AI Research Agents Narrow Scientific Exploration
finding: AI ideas sit in lower-impact regions, and more of their novelty is method recombination than new problems.
numbers: Impact score is the mean normalised citation of neighbouring papers; AI lower than the human area baseline. Field table shows modifying or recombining methods is more common than finding new problems; Sociology and Business higher on new problems.
limits: Impact proxied by neighbour citations, not the idea's own outcome.
agent_relevance: Local elaboration is the default LLM mode; Fleming's familiar-parts advantage shows up as safe but low-impact output.

source: Liu, Butler, Machlanski, Bueno, Tsaftaris (2026) Large Language Models Extend Known Research But Do Not Create New Research Directions
finding: Two kinds of novelty split. Distance from the nearest paper is larger for LLM hypotheses, but direction (orthogonal novelty score, ONS) is lower than for real papers.
numbers: 26.9 million papers, 1,325 topics, 524,308 hypotheses, 8 LLMs, 20 focal papers per prompt. Median ONS 15-23% lower than real papers; real paper has higher ONS in 72-82% of random pairs; effect in 86-97% of topics. ONS win rate 18-28% vs 35-48% on centroid distance.
limits: SPECTER2 embedding geometry; ONS is a new metric by the authors.
agent_relevance: Recombining far parts is not a new direction. Track direction separately from distance in any novelty check.

source: Liu, Butler, Machlanski, Bueno, Tsaftaris (2026) Large Language Models Extend Known Research But Do Not Create New Research Directions
finding: Context choice changes distance but not direction. Feeding the 20 papers farthest from the topic centre pushes hypotheses outward; the number of papers and larger models do not fix direction.
numbers: Farthest-paper context: 11-12% further from centroid and 16% further from nearest paper than real papers (win rate 77-84%). Focal papers N=5 to 100: no change; ONS 16-18% lower at every N. ONS under farthest context: GPT-5.4-nano win rate 39%, Gemini-3.1-Flash-Lite 45% (n.s.). Larger models: Gemini ONS win rate 26% to 22%.
limits: Two small models for the context tests, 86 topics.
agent_relevance: Feeding far components into context is the one lever that moved distance. It is cheap and can be done by code in O7.

source: Liu, Butler, Machlanski, Bueno, Tsaftaris (2026) Large Language Models Extend Known Research But Do Not Create New Research Directions (multi-turn refinement section)
finding: Abstract says the contraction persists across context, persona and judge-dialogue configurations. The refinement figures were not read in detail.
numbers: Abstract-level only: contraction persists across configurations.
limits: Not opened beyond the abstract and the context sections.
agent_relevance: Do not assume a refinement loop alone fixes direction.

source: Scideator (2024) Human-LLM Scientific Ideation through Facet Recombination and Novelty Evaluation
finding: Tool that splits papers into purpose, mechanism and evaluation facets, pairs a purpose from one paper with a mechanism from another at near, far or very far distance, and checks novelty against literature. Facet-aware retrieval is the key to the checker.
numbers: User study N=22 CS researchers, within-subject, more creativity support than a strong baseline (scores not in the text read). Novelty checker ablation on 58 ideas (recall of not-novel): full 89.66%, facet-agnostic RankGPT 13.79%, embedding only 10.34%, keywords 5.17%. Expert set 67 labelled (39 novel, 28 not); best accuracy 0.81, F1 0.79, kappa 0.59; AI Scientist 0.47. Per generation 6 candidate analogies, keep 2; 4 ideas.
limits: Small expert set; ablations on not-novel cases only; titles and abstracts only; CS only.
agent_relevance: A working facet-recombination loop with distance bands exists. Fixed distance bands plus a literature novelty check is a ready design for O7.

source: Scideator (2024) Human-LLM Scientific Ideation through Facet Recombination and Novelty Evaluation
finding: Distance labels in the tool agreed only moderately with annotators.
numbers: Facet-distance annotation kappa = 0.53 and 0.61; novelty annotation kappa = 0.68.
limits: Moderate agreement means near, far and very far labels are noisy.
agent_relevance: Use computed embedding distance, not an LLM label, for distance bands.

source: Wang et al. (2023) SciMON: Scientific Inspiration Machines Optimized for Novelty
finding: Retrieval of inspiration from knowledge-graph, semantic and citation neighbours, plus an iterative novelty loop (revise until similarity to prior work is under 0.6), raises novelty. Output is often a generic recombination of popular concepts.
numbers: 67,408 ACL papers; novelty loop k=20, threshold 0.6. First iteration: 55.6% of ideas gained novelty with semantic-neighbour inspiration (88.9% substantially different); second iteration raised novelty for 57.8% of continuing ideas. GPT-4 few-shot novelty gain +54.4%. Human helpfulness: GPT-4 FS 73%, GPT-4 FS+KG 66%, T5+SN 48%. Ground truth rated more novel in 85% of comparisons.
limits: Seed terms came from the gold output; raters PhD students; relation extraction precision 65.4%; GPT-4 outputs longer.
agent_relevance: A novelty loop with a numeric similarity cut-off is cheap and code-checkable. KG inspirations did not beat plain GPT-4 few-shot on helpfulness.

source: Chen, Zhang (2026) Enhancing Research Idea Generation through Combinatorial Innovation and Multi-Agent Iterative Search Strategies
finding: Multi-agent iterative search over paper-derived knowledge. Early rounds import new entities and later rounds lock in to the previous version; diversity and novelty peak near the second iteration while quality keeps rising.
numbers: 144 target ACL 2024 papers, 6,000+ references. Diversity 0.898, novelty 0.133. Entity analysis: turn 1 70.6% new; turn 2 43.1% inherited from previous version; turn 3 78.3% inherited. Teams of 5-7 gave higher quality but lower diversity. Ideas beat rejected ICLR 2025 papers (p<0.001), not accepted ones.
limits: Baseline numbers not on the page read; LLM ranker only; NLP only. Authors note superficial novelty (too many subproblems merged).
agent_relevance: Matches the reuse penalty: repeated refinement locks into one combination. Cap refinement rounds near two and branch again.

source: Ramon Llull-style combinatorial ideation over theme, domain and method disks (2025)
finding: Systematic enumeration of element triples gives high diversity when sampled at random, but relevance falls. Top-frequency elements give the opposite.
numbers: 7,483 papers merged; 682 themes, 633 domains, 866 methods, 925 templates. Diversity (distinct-1): Random 0.41, Top 0.21, baselines 0.29 and 0.29. Relevance (BLEU): Random 0.05, Top 0.11, baselines 0.28 and 0.18. Title reconstruction from elements 16.4% at Jaccard >=0.30. Year-to-year element overlap (Jaccard): method 0.05-0.09.
limits: Metrics do not measure merit; no human evaluation; no distance or combination-size ablation. Authors not named in the page read.
agent_relevance: Reproduces Fleming's trade in a machine setting: random far parts add spread and lose relevance. No quality check, so it shows only half of the trade.

source: Li, Tu, Han (2026) Graph2Idea: Retrieval-Augmented Scientific Idea Generation with Graph-Structured Contexts
finding: Compact graph context from retrieved papers plus a direction-planning step improves automatic novelty, quality and feasibility together.
numbers: Novelty / rel. quality / rel. feasibility: Graph2Idea 0.52 / 0.29 / 0.28; AI-Researcher 0.45 / 0.24 / 0.22; MAGenIdeas 0.20 / 0.19 / 0.06; AI-Scientist 0.09 / 0.12 / 0.19. Ablations: no direction 0.47, no strategy and direction 0.48, no graph context 0.50.
limits: All proxy metrics from LLM judges (novelty = not covered in top-10 retrieved papers); authors say these are not validity.
agent_relevance: Small ablation gaps (0.50 vs 0.52 for graph context) suggest direction planning matters more than graph form.

source: Jiang (2026) HINDSIGHT: Evaluating LLM-Generated Research Ideas via Future Impact
finding: Judge by outcome, not by sound. LLM judges see no difference between retrieval-grounded and vanilla ideas; matching to real later papers shows a 2.5x gap. LLM-rated novelty correlates negatively with real impact.
numbers: 200 ideas (100 vs 100), 10 topics, 30-month window. LLM-judge overall 7.44 vs 7.40 (p=0.584). HINDSIGHT mean 0.297 vs 0.119 (p<0.001). Correlation of HINDSIGHT score with LLM-judged novelty = -0.29 (p<0.01).
limits: AI/ML topics only; matching to future papers can miss good ideas nobody wrote.
agent_relevance: Fleming measured usefulness by later citations; this is the one LLM study that copies that logic. Never select on LLM-rated novelty alone (see G5, G8).

source: Bao, Wu, Liu, Li, Cao, Evans (2026) Contemporary AI lacks the imagination to diverge or negate in science
finding: Authors rated LLM ideas derived from their own papers. Non-reasoning LLMs share a hivemind of similar ideas; reasoning models spread wider; no model proposes null hypotheses unprompted. Scientists prefer ideas like their own and weigh probability over novelty. Retrieval and persona prompts give marginal gains.
numbers: Authors of 121,640 preprints invited; 6,749 scientists returned 25,139 rating sets. A Qwen3-14B reward model trained on ratings beat SOTA judges by up to 27%. Analysis of 39 million papers 2010-2025: null claims suppressed after ChatGPT release.
limits: Survey self-selection; ratings of ideas, not executed work.
agent_relevance: Familiar-looking ideas win expert ratings, echoing Fleming's familiarity premium. Mixing reasoning and non-reasoning draws helps spread.

source: Ye, Liu (2025) U2F: Encouraging SWE-Agent to Seize Novelty without Losing Feasibility
finding: Software-agent scaffold that explores unknown solution paths using cross-domain analogies, then integrates to keep feasibility. Novelty rises step by step with more scaffold.
numbers: Novelty: zero-shot 2.85, role prompting 3.20, SE analysis prompt 3.55, U2F 4.05 (42.1% over zero-shot; 14% over SEAP). Semantic novelty 0.28 to 0.68 vs zero-shot. Feasibility 4.02/5. 1.55 unknown unknowns per case. Expert approval 62%. 15 experts, Fleiss kappa 0.65; human-LLM Pearson 0.81 (novelty).
limits: Authors' own benchmark; small expert panel; the evaluator is also an LLM.
agent_relevance: Example of a cross-domain analogy step inside an agent loop, with feasibility kept by an integration stage after exploration.

source: Peeperkorn et al. (2024), cited in Mizrahi et al. (2025)
finding: Claim from a citing paper: higher temperature correlates only weakly with novelty and its influence on creativity is subtle and limited.
numbers: No numbers read; cited secondhand in the Mizrahi et al. introduction.
limits: Not opened; secondhand.
agent_relevance: Do not use temperature as the main variation lever; use structured recombination.
